Obtaining and Extracting the Source\n\nDownload three archives from the POV-Ray official archive at `https://www.povray.org/ftp/pub/povray/Old-Versions/Official-2.2/`:\n\n- **POVDOC.TAR.Z** (documentation + include files)\n- **POVSCN.TAR.Z** (example scenes)\n- **POVSRC.TAR.Z** (source code)\n\nExtract all three to a location of your choice. On Linux, you'd use something like:\n```\nzcat POVDOC.TAR.Z | tar xvf -\nzcat POVSCN.TAR.Z | tar xvf -\nzcat POVSRC.TAR.Z | tar xvf -\n```\n\n## 2. Install Build Prerequisites\n\nOn Debian/Ubuntu and derivatives, install the build tools:\n\n```\napt install build-essential\n```\n\nThis brings in GCC and GNU Make. (BSD users should use **gmake** instead of make.)\n\n## 3. Set Up the Build Directory\n\nInside the extracted **POVSRC** directory, you'll find two folders: **`machine`** and **`source`**.\n\n- Copy **all files** from `machine/unix/` (but not the `unix` directory itself) into the **`source`** folder.\n- In the **`source`** folder, rename **`unixconf.h`** to **`config.h`**.\n\n## 4. Patch 1: Fix Random Number Generation (Critical)\n\nThe default system RNG causes two problems: non-deterministic renders across platforms, and sometimes crashes/aborts during rendering.\n\n**To fix:** Open `machine/ibmpc/ibm.c` and go to approximately **line 2784**, where you'll find this ANSI Standard pseudo-random number generator:\n\n```c\n/* ANSI Standard pseudo-random number generator */\n\nint rand(void);\nvoid srand(int);\n\nstatic unsigned long int next = 1;\n\nint rand()\n   {\n   next = next * 1103515245L + 12345L;\n   return ((int) (next / 0x10000L) & 0x7FFF);\n   }\n\nvoid srand(seed)\n   int seed;\n   {\n   next = (unsigned long int)seed;\n   }\n```\n\nCopy this entire block. Then open **`source/unix.c`** and **paste this code at the very end of the file**. Save the file.\n\nThis overrides the system RNG calls with a deterministic generator, ensuring consistent output across operating systems and preventing crashes.\n\n## 5. Patch 2: Enable Extra Optimization\n\nOpen **`source/unix.mak`** and locate **line 21**:\n\n```\nCFLAGS=\t\t-c -O\nLFLAGS =\t-o povray -O\n```\n\nChange the **`-O`** flag to **`-O2`** on **both** lines:\n\n```\nCFLAGS=\t\t-c -O2\nLFLAGS =\t-o povray -O2\n```\n\nThis enables level 2 optimization. The guide notes that level 3 (`-O3`) \"can sometimes cause bugs or even sacrifice performance compared to level 2.\"\n\n## 6. Patch 3: Increase MAX_CONSTANTS (Optional but Recommended)\n\nThe default limit of 1000 `#declare` constants will cause a \"Too many constants\" error for complex scenes. In **`source/unix.mak`** at line 21, the CFLAGS line should now read `CFLAGS= -c -O2`. Add a `-D` macro definition:\n\n```\nCFLAGS=\t\t-c -O2 -DMAX_CONSTANTS=2000\n```\n\nThis sets the limit to 2000 (adjustable to your needs; higher values use more memory).\n\n## 7. Compile\n\nFrom within the **`source`** directory, run:\n\n```\nmake -f unix.mak\n```\n\nFor multi-core builds, append `-jX` where X equals your core/thread count:\n\n```\nmake -f unix.mak -j8\n```\n\nCompilation warnings will appear on screen — the guide says \"these can be ignored as they don't cause any issues.\"\n\n## 8. Make the Binary Executable\n\nAfter compilation succeeds, a file called **`povray`** is produced:\n\n```\nchmod +x povray\n```\n\nVerify it works:\n\n```\n./povray\n```\n\nYou should see authorship and usage information.\n\n## 9. Install to PATH (Optional)\n\nCreate a local bin directory if needed:\n\n```\nmkdir -p ~/.local/bin/\n```\n\nCopy the binary there, optionally renaming it to avoid conflicts with modern POV-Ray:\n\n```\ncp povray ~/.local/bin/povray2\n```\n\nLog out and back in if the directory was newly created, so your PATH updates.\n\n## 10. Rendering\n\nYou need the **`include`** directory from inside POVDOC. To render a scene, e.g. `planet.pov` from the scenes archive:\n\n```\npovray2 +L<location of include directory> +Iplanet.pov +Oplanet.tga +FT +W640 +H480 +A0.1 +V\n```\n\n| Flag | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| `+L` | Include file search path |\n| `+I` | Input scene file |\n| `+O` | Output image filename |\n| `+F` | Image format (`T` = TARGA/TGA) |\n| `+W` | Image width in pixels |\n| `+H` | Image height in pixels |\n| `+A` | Anti-aliasing threshold |\n| `+V` | Verbose output |\n\n## Summary of All Source Changes\n\n1. **Copy** `machine/unix/*` → `source/`\n2. **Rename** `source/unixconf.h` → `source/config.h`\n3. **Append** the IBM PC deterministic RNG code (from `machine/ibmpc/ibm.c` ~line 2784) to the end of `source/unix.c`\n4. **Edit** `source/unix.mak` line 21: change `-O` to `-O2` on both CFLAGS and LFLAGS lines, and add `-DMAX_CONSTANTS=2000` to CFLAGS"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"c1310ba9-a9f5-41bd-9959-cc285ed39f5e","uuid":"8c793fab-748c-418d-b85f-c68fcd8221d0","timestamp":"2026-08-10T10:20:06.205Z","tool_use_result":{"bytes":20414,"code":200,"codeText":"OK","result":"# Compiling POV-Ray 2.2 from Source on Modern Linux\n\n## 1.
